Xray process state change. Fired when Xray starts, stops, or encounters an error; state is running, stop or error, and errorMsg carries the reason when it is error.
In-panel toast notification. Fired on Xray stop/restart, DB import, panel restart, etc. level is success, info, warning or error.

Instructs the UI to re-fetch a resource. Fired when another admin session modifies data (e.g. toggling inbound enable). The payload names the message type whose cached data is stale: inbounds, outbounds, nodes or clients.

info.title: P-UI Panel API
info.description: Programmatic interface to a Penhoon UI (P-UI) panel. Authenticate with a session cookie or Bearer token. Administrator operations require administrator access; read-only tokens cannot mutate state or export protected configuration. Reseller tokens are restricted to their own account, clients, granted inbounds and permitted private plans. Token expiry and source-address restrictions also apply.

bearerAuth.description: API token from Panel Settings → API Token or a reseller account. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Role, scope, expiry and source-address restrictions apply.

cookieAuth.name: p-ui
cookieAuth.description: Session cookie set by POST /login. Browser-only.

Zero and "" are what a form that predates these posts; the service reads

smtpLastError.description: SmtpLastError and SmtpLastErrorAt are written by the mailer and shown read-only.

BanView.description:
BanView is a ban as the panel lists it: the row, and the name of the node it
is held on, "" for this host.

Capabilities.description:
Capabilities is what a core claims it can do. Every field is a *bool because
nil means UNKNOWN, which is a normal state: a master talking to a node one
release behind cannot distinguish "cannot" from "was never asked".

Client.description: Client represents a client configuration for Xray inbounds with traffic limits and settings.

preSharedKey.description: Omit to keep the stored key, send empty to clear it

tlsCryptV2.description: OpenVPN wrapped client key, per inbound

username.description: Login name for a core that takes one (SSH)

ClientBan.description:
/*
ClientBan is one device over its cap, dropped on the firewall of the host that
serves the client until Until. Active rows only: the row is the memory that the
pair is banned and the source the firewall set is projected from, and it leaves
when its deadline passes or an operator releases it.

NodeGuid is "" for a ban this host holds itself. Ports is the CSV of local
inbound ports the ban covers, or "*" for every local inbound port, resolved
each pass, which is what an operator's own ban of an address means.
*/

createdAt.description: Unix seconds, the unit every synced timestamp in this panel carries.

origin.description:
Origin is "" for a ban this panel decided, or the guid of the master
that pushed it, which is the only one whose push may end it.

ClientConfigFile.description:
ClientConfigFile is one importable client config: what to call the file, and
what is in it.

preSharedKey.description: Omit to keep the stored key, send empty to clear it

tlsCryptV2.description: OpenVPN wrapped client key, per inbound

username.description: Login name for a core that takes one (SSH)

ClientLocalAddress.description:
/*
ClientLocalAddress is one address a client answers to inside a tunnel, and the
core that reported it.

Per core rather than merged, because the answer differs per protocol and the two
are only comparable within one: two clients can reach each other over the address
they hold on the SAME inbound, and never across cores.
*/

ClientPageResponse.description:
ClientPageResponse is the shape returned by ListPaged. `Total` is the
row count in the DB; `Filtered` is the count after Search/Filter/Protocol
were applied, before pagination. The page contains at most PageSize items.
Summary is computed across the full DB row set so dashboard counters
on the clients page stay stable as the user paginates/filters.

ClientPolicy.description: Assignments use email so a node re-sync that changes the client id preserves them.

appliedRev.description:
AppliedRev is what the PANEL's own writes reached, never what a node holds.
Node convergence rides MarkNodeDirtyTx and the pending indicator that exists.

overrideQuota.description:
The bit IS the override, and only explicit operator intent sets it. The value
itself lives on the client, so it cannot be inferred by comparing to the plan.

policyId.description:
PolicyId is nullable and the FK is ON DELETE SET NULL, not CASCADE: deleting
a plan must leave the assignment visible-and-unresolved for the UI to report.

resolvedTiers.description:
ResolvedTiers is the ladder as the master that owns this client evaluated
it, pushed to a node; NULL wherever the plan itself lives (policy_id).

ClientSlim.description:
ClientSlim is the row-shape used by the clients page. It drops fields the
table never reads (UUID, password, auth, flow, security, reverse, tgId)
so the list payload stays compact even when the panel manages thousands
of clients. Modals that need the full record still call /get/:email.

disabledReason.description: DisabledReason is "quota", "expiry" or "manual" while Enable is false.

ClientTraffic.description:
ClientTraffic is the per-client usage row. It is keyed by email and shared by
every inbound a client uses, which is what makes one quota span every core.

ClientsSummary.description:
ClientsSummary collects per-bucket counts plus the matching email lists so
the clients page can render the dashboard stat cards and their hover
popovers without shipping the full client array. The counters are exact;
the lists stop at clientSummaryEmailCap entries and only back the popovers.

CoreStatusView.description:
/*
CoreStatusView is one core as the Cores page shows it: what runs, whether it
answers, and which build is installed. Polled — unlike CoreView, which the
frontend fetches once because it changes only with the binary.

State and Ready are core.Health.Overall's, so the page, the event pass and the
conformance suite agree on what degraded means; a core that reports no health
says "unknown" rather than guessing.
*/

available.description: Available is this host's Preflight answer and Unavailable is why not.

healthError.example: singbox: inbound 4: supervisor: list p-ui-singbox-4.service: dbus: connection closed

hostRuntime.description: HostRuntime observes matching daemon processes without adopting them.

instances.description:
Instances are the per-inbound daemons of a core that runs one each; a
single-process core lists none and fills the fields above instead.

logs.description: Logs says TailLog is available for this core, so the page offers the drawer.

state.description:
State is running, degraded, stopped, failed, idle or unknown; Ready says
the daemon answers on its control surface; Detail is why not, or the last exit.

trafficSeenAt.description:
TrafficSeenAt is when this core last reported traffic (Unix ms, 0 = not
since start) and TrafficError why the last poll failed, if it did.

unavailable.example: ocserv: stat /usr/sbin/ocserv: no such file (apt-get install ocserv)

CoreVersionsView.description:
CoreVersionsView is a core's release picture: the build on disk and, when the
core can install one, the channel's list.

error.description: Error is why Installed or Available is missing; a missing binary is one.

CoreView.description:
CoreView is one registered core as the UI sees it. Kinds is []string rather
than []core.Kind: openapigen emits none of the core contract's own type names.

applyDelaySeconds.description:
ApplyDelaySeconds, per kind, is how long an edit takes to land on a core
that applies on its next pass; a kind absent here applies at once.

available.description:
Available is this host's Preflight answer and Unavailable is why not, so a
core the host cannot run is explained rather than silently offered.

clientCredentials.description:
ClientCredentials are the credential fields a client of each kind carries,
keyed by kind. A kind absent here declares none; the form keeps its own.

exitKinds.description:
ExitKinds are the kinds a route may terminate on — the outbound half of
Kinds, so an outbound picker is built from the registry rather than a list.

ipLimitEnforcement.description:
/*
		IpLimitEnforcement says, per kind, how a device over its cap is dealt with:
		"login" — refused at the core's own login and cut, no firewall needed;
		"cut" — cut by the core and dropped on the panel's ban set, since it admits
		at no login; "firewall" — the ban set alone. A kind absent here cannot be
		capped at all. The form gates the cap on this rather than on the firewall
		alone: a cap on an SSH client holds where the set cannot be written, and
		one on Xray does not.
	*/

kinds.description:
Kinds are the inbound protocols this core serves; a core may serve many,
so the id is not a protocol and must never be used as one.

portlessKinds.description:
/*
		PortlessKinds are the kinds that bind no port at all — an Xray TUN device
		is a kernel interface, not a listener.

		The form asks this instead of asking a protocol list, so it stops
		demanding a port for one, and the port-conflict check stops counting the
		stored value as occupied. Asked with no settings on purpose: whether a
		kind binds anything is not a property of one inbound's configuration. F319.
	*/

rateKinds.description:
RateKinds are the kinds whose core throttles each client inside itself, so
a plan's rates reach them without a kernel identity. Shaping's complement.

sessionKinds.description:
/*
		SessionKinds are the kinds whose core can name each live connection and the
		address it came from — the one thing an IP limit is decided from.

		A kind absent here cannot have a cap enforced however the form is filled
		in: EvaluateIPLimits only ever sees clients a core reported a session for,
		and a core that reports a user in use and no address cannot report one.
		The form says so instead of accepting a number that does nothing. F120 / F302.
	*/

shaping.description:
Shaping names the kernel key each kind's clients carry, so a form gates its
speed fields on this. A kind absent here cannot be rate limited at all.

trafficSeenAt.description:
TrafficSeenAt is when this core last reported traffic (Unix ms, 0 = not
since start) and TrafficError why the last poll failed, if it did.

unavailable.example: wireguard: no kernel support on this host

Diag.description:
Diag is what the operator is told about one (rule, subject) pair.

Per PAIR and never per row: one rule naming an Xray inbound and a WireGuard
inbound is realised by two different mechanisms, and one chip cannot describe
both without lying about one of them.

Egress.description:
/*
Egress is one policy-routed exit an L3 inbound's traffic can be sent out through.

Id is the only allocation this row stores: the routing table, the ip rule
priority, the front device and its gateway are all pure functions of it, so a
freed id must never come back while any of that kernel state can still exist.
Type is the whole generalisation seam — one driver per value — and Settings is
the per-type column that buys the next driver zero migrations.
*/

enable.description:
Enable carries no column default on purpose: GORM omits a false from the
INSERT when one exists, so "create it disabled" would silently enable it.

ingressInboundId.description:
IngressInboundId is the inbound this front exists for, UNIQUE so the one
front per ingress rule is the schema's rather than a convention.

owner.description:
Owner distinguishes a front the panel provisions for an ingress from an
uplink an operator named. A panel row legitimately carries no target.

target.description:
Target is the outbound or balancer tag the front sends traffic to. An
unresolvable one leaves the egress dark — contained, never silently direct.

EnforcedLimits.description:
EnforcedLimits is one client's answer: the plan the rules derive, and what the
kernel is actually holding. They differ exactly when something did not land.

policyId.description:
PolicyId is 0 when the client is on no plan; Unresolved means the row names
a plan that no longer exists, which never throttles and must be reported.

rateEnforced.description:
RateEnforced reports that a core throttling in-process holds a limit for this
client NOW, read back from that core; Shapeable's complement.

shapeable.description:
Shapeable reports whether the kernel holds state for this client NOW, which
needs a core that can identify them and a plan granting them a rate.

usedBytes.description: UsedBytes is the same number the quota is enforced against.

ExternalLinkInput.description: ExternalLinkInput is one row from the client form's Links tab.

FallbackParentInfo.description:
FallbackParentInfo carries everything the frontend needs to rewrite a
child inbound's client link: where to connect (the master's address
and port) and which path matched on the master's fallbacks array.
The frontend already has the master inbound in its dbInbounds list,
so we only ship identifiers + the match path here.

HistoryOfSeeders.description: HistoryOfSeeders tracks which database seeders have been executed to prevent re-running.

downloadSettings.description:
/*
		DownloadSettings overrides the XHTTP split-download endpoint for this
		host, as a JSON object of the same shape the inbound stores.

		A host is a different way in to the same inbound, and only the upload
		half moves with it: without this, the alternate entry point uploads to
		the host's address while still downloading from the inbound's original
		one. Empty = inherit the inbound's endpoint. Free-form JSON like the
		three above, so a future core with its own second endpoint reuses the
		column rather than adding one.
	*/

finalMask.description:
FinalMask is a JSON object of xray finalmask masks (tcp/udp/quicParams),
merged into this host's JSON-subscription stream. Empty = no override.

mihomoX25519.description:
Deprecated: read by nothing, and it never could be. The Clash renderer
already emits reality-opts.public-key for every REALITY proxy, so this
could only ever have switched correct output off. Still stored and
returned; scheduled for removal in a future release. F141.

shuffleHost.description:
Deprecated: read by nothing. Shuffling is a property of the proxy LIST,
not of one member of it, so a per-host flag could not express it; the
feature now lives in the subscription setting subClashShuffleProxies.
Still stored and returned; scheduled for removal in a future release. F141.

vlessRoute.description:
Single VLESS route value (0-65535) baked into the subscription UUID's 3rd
group (bytes 6-7), which xray reads via net.PortFromBytes(id[6:8]). Empty = none.

mihomoX25519.description:
Deprecated: read by nothing; the Clash renderer already emits
reality-opts.public-key for every REALITY proxy. See model.Host. F141.

shuffleHost.description:
Deprecated: read by nothing; shuffling moved to the subscription setting
subClashShuffleProxies, because order belongs to the list. See model.Host. F141.

Inbound.description: Inbound represents an Xray inbound configuration with traffic statistics and settings.

egressId.description:
EgressID selects the Egress this inbound leaves through. A column, not a
settings key: settings-borne selection forces a REALITY inbound to restart.

fallbackParent.description:
FallbackParent is populated by the API layer when this inbound is
attached as a fallback child of a VLESS/Trojan TCP-TLS master.
The frontend uses it to rewrite client-share links so they advertise
the master's externally reachable endpoint instead of the child's
loopback listen. Not persisted.

originNodeGuid.description:
OriginNodeGuid is the panelGuid of the node that physically hosts this
inbound, propagated up across hops (#4983). Empty for an inbound that
lives on this panel's own xray; set to the originating node's GUID when
the inbound was synced from a node (kept as-is across further hops). Lets
the master attribute a deeply nested inbound to the real node instead of
the intermediate one it was fetched through.

subSortIndex.description: 1-based sort order of this inbound's links in subscription output only (lower first; ties by id)

trafficResetDay.description: Day of month for monthly traffic resets

InboundClientIps.description: InboundClientIps stores IP addresses associated with inbound clients for access control.

nodeAddress.description:
Share-host resolution inputs, mirroring the subscription's
resolveInboundAddress so the clients page renders a node-managed WireGuard
Endpoint that points at the node, not the master panel. NodeAddress is the
hosting node's externally reachable address (empty for this panel's own
inbounds); Listen and ShareAddrStrategy/ShareAddr feed the same
node→listen→custom fallback the share/QR links already use.

nodeId.description:
Hosting node; nil for this panel's own inbounds. Lets the clients
page map a node filter onto inbound IDs (#4997).

InstanceStatusView.description: InstanceStatusView is one daemon of a per-inbound core.

detail.example: the management socket is not open yet

IpLimitStatus.description:
/*
IpLimitStatus tells the frontend whether a device over its cap can be dropped on
this host: Enforceable is whether the panel's own ban table can be written,
Reason why not, and Enabled whether banning is turned on here at all.
*/

MetricSample.description:
MetricSample is one point of any time-series we keep in memory.
The frontend deserializes both keys, so they must stay short.

warning.description:
Warning carries a post-commit failure: the write landed, something after it
did not, and no retry of the write will repair it.

Node.description:
Node represents a remote Penhoon UI panel registered with the central panel.
The central panel polls each node's existing /panel/api/server/status
endpoint over HTTP using the per-node ApiToken to populate the runtime
status fields below.

guid.description:
Guid is the remote panel's stable self-identifier (its panelGuid),
learned from each heartbeat. It is the globally stable node identity used
to attribute online clients/inbounds to the physical node across a chain
of nodes (#4983); panel-local autoincrement ids don't survive a hop.
Observed-state only — never user-edited.

parentGuid.description:
ParentGuid + Transitive are set only when a node is surfaced as part of a
node tree (#4983): direct nodes carry the master panel's own GUID, a
transitive sub-node carries its parent node's GUID. Transitive nodes are
read-only projections (Id == 0, not persisted) — never edited or deployed.

status.description:
Heartbeat-updated fields. UpdatedAt advances on every probe even when
the row is otherwise unchanged so the UI's "last seen" tooltip is
truthful without us having to read LastHeartbeat separately.
online|offline|unknown

xrayState.description:
XrayState and XrayError are captured from the remote node's /panel/api/server/status
during heartbeats. They let the central panel distinguish "panel API reachable"
(status=online) from "Xray core itself has failed on the node" for monitoring.

NodeMutationRequest.description:
NodeMutationRequest is the node write/probe contract. ApiToken is accepted
only as input. On update, nil means keep the stored token; replacement and
clearing are explicit and mutually exclusive.

NodeView.description:
NodeView is the browser/API read contract for nodes. Credentials are
write-only: responses expose only whether a node has a token configured.

OutboundTraffics.description: OutboundTraffics tracks traffic statistics for Xray outbound connections.

PanelUpdateStatus.description:
PanelUpdateStatus reports the outcome of the most recently launched panel
self-update. RunID lets the caller confirm this status belongs to the
update it started rather than a stale result left over from an earlier
run; State is one of "pending", "success", or "failed". RunID is a decimal
string, not a JSON number: it's a formatted UnixNano timestamp, and
JavaScript's number type can't represent that precisely (it exceeds
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), which would let two different runs round to the
same value on the wire and defeat the whole point of this field.

Policy.description: Policy is a reusable client template; its speed ladder remains live on edits.

quotaBytes.description:
NULL means the plan does not manage the field; 0 means managed and unlimited.
Both states are needed, or the first edit of a ladder-only plan wipes members.

rev.description:
Rev bumps only when a managed field or the inbound set changes, so editing a
ladder lights no pending badge. client_policies.applied_rev chases it.

tiers.description:
Tiers is a policy.Tier array. Sorted and de-duplicated on write, so the
evaluation on every pass is a scan and never a sort.

xrayState.description:
XrayState/XrayError are populated on successful probes even when the node's
Xray core is not healthy. The UI uses them for a distinct "panel ok, xray failed" indicator.

onDepletion.description: Only the traffic axis is soft: block refuses new provisioning and keeps clients online.

periodStartedAt.description: The cycle anchor: set when a cycle is switched on and at every usage reset.

trafficAllocated.description: Projected from the allocation ledger; the old column stays for schema compatibility.

sales.description: The existing response key holds committed quota reservations, not payment events.

RoutingExitView.description:
/*
RoutingExitView is one uplink as the rule editor offers it.

The handle is deliberately not here: which device or port realises an exit is
the compile's business, and an editor that showed it would invite an operator to
depend on it.
*/

RoutingRule.description:
/*
RoutingRule is one row of operator intent: these inbounds, these criteria, this
destination.

Keyed on inbound IDs rather than tags, which is what makes a rule immune to the
tag-rewriting an inbound rename or delete performs — the failure mode that used
to widen a rule to every inbound on the box.
*/

ingressScope.description:
IngressScope is "selected" or "all"; "all" expands at compile time to one
rule per routable subject, in this rule's own position.

RoutingSubject.description:
RoutingSubject is one inbound as a routing rule may name it. An unroutable tag
is offered disabled with ReasonKey, never hidden — hiding it reads as data loss.

RoutingSubjectView.description:
RoutingSubjectView is one inbound as the editor offers it, with the reason it
cannot be named when it cannot.

RuleView.description:
/*
RuleView is a stored rule plus what the last config generation made of it.

The rule is embedded rather than nested so the list keeps the shape it has
always had and a client that ignores diags is unaffected.
*/

diags.description:
Diags carries the refusals for this rule from the last generate, one per
(rule, subject) pair. Empty means the rule is realised, or that no config
has been generated since this process started.

ingressScope.description:
IngressScope is "selected" or "all"; "all" expands at compile time to one
rule per routable subject, in this rule's own position.

SSHHostKey.description: SSHHostKey is what an SSH server presented, for the operator to pin.

Setting.description: Setting stores key-value configuration settings for the Penhoon UI panel.

Status.description:
Status represents comprehensive system and application status information.
It includes CPU, memory, disk, network statistics, and Xray process status.

User.description: User represents a user account in the Penhoon UI panel.

VersionStatusView.description:
VersionStatusView is what is installed and whether the panel may change it.
Reported is false for a core that names no version at all.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: UI sessions use a cookie set by the login endpoint. Programmatic clients authenticate with a Bearer token from Panel Settings → API Token or their reseller account. Each operation enforces the authenticated role, token scope and ownership. The global WebSocket requires an administrator session cookie.

tags.name: Inbounds
tags.description: Manage inbound configurations and their clients. All endpoints live under /panel/api/inbounds and require a logged-in session or Bearer token. Link-generating endpoints honour forwarded headers only when the request comes from a configured trusted proxy.

tags.name: Server
tags.description: System status, log retrieval, certificate generators, Xray binary management, and backup/restore. All under /panel/api/server.

tags.name: Clients
tags.description: Manage clients as first-class entities that can be attached to one or more inbounds. A single client row drives the settings.clients entry in every inbound it belongs to. Endpoints live under /panel/api/clients.

tags.name: Nodes
tags.description: Manage remote Penhoon UI panels acting as nodes for a central panel. All endpoints under /panel/api/nodes.

tags.name: Routing
tags.description: Operator routing intent: which inbounds, which criteria, which destination. A rule names inbounds by ID rather than by tag, so renaming or deleting an inbound cannot silently widen it to every inbound on the box. The compile decides which mechanism realises each rule -- an Xray inbound is named directly, while a kernel inbound is fronted and its rule rewritten onto the front's tag -- which is what lets one screen route any protocol to any protocol. A rule naming an inbound the router cannot see is refused at save rather than accepted and left to never match. All endpoints under /panel/api/routing.

tags.name: Egresses
tags.description: A policy-routed exit an L3 inbound's traffic leaves through. The panel owns one ip rule per attached inbound, a private routing table and its blackhole; the front device belongs to the core the egress type names. Everything the kernel needs is derived from the egress id, so an id is never reused. ICMP is answered by the front itself, so a ping or traceroute through an egress succeeds for any destination whatsoever, including one nothing could reach — test an egress with a TCP or UDP request instead. Master-local: an inbound assigned to a node cannot be attached yet. All endpoints under /panel/api/egresses.

tags.name: Policies
tags.description: Reusable client plans combine traffic quotas, duration, device limits, inbound assignments and speed tiers. Template changes are tracked separately from applied client settings; reapply updates members while preserving explicit overrides unless requested otherwise. Quota continuation, renewal and rate shaping are validated against each core capability. Zero bits per second means unlimited in that direction. Administrator plans use /panel/api/policies; permitted resellers manage their own plans under /panel/api/reseller/plans.

tags.name: Hosts
tags.description: Per-inbound override endpoints. Each enabled host renders one extra subscription link/proxy with its own address/port/TLS, superseding the legacy externalProxy array. All endpoints under /panel/api/hosts.

tags.name: Backup
tags.description: PostgreSQL snapshots, retention, scheduled backups, authenticated encryption for manual archives, restore operations and optional delivery to configured administrator Telegram chats. Backups and protected configuration require administrator write access.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Panel configuration and user credentials. All endpoints live under /panel/api/setting and require a logged-in session or Bearer token.

tags.name: API Tokens
tags.description: Manage administrator Bearer tokens for automation. Tokens have a name, enabled flag, scope, expiry and optional source-IP/CIDR restrictions. Disabling or deleting a token revokes it. Tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes; plaintext is returned only at creation. Send one as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Read-only tokens cannot change state or export protected configuration. Reseller tokens are managed separately and retain their account ownership and permissions.

tags.name: Xray Settings
tags.description: Xray configuration template, outbound management, Warp/Nord integration, and config testing. All endpoints under /panel/api/xray.

tags.name: Subscription Server
tags.description: A separate HTTP/HTTPS server that serves proxy subscription links (standard, JSON, and Clash) to clients. The server listens on its own port (default 2096) and is configured in Settings → Subscription. Paths are configurable; defaults are shown below. Subscription responses include traffic/expiry headers; individual configuration-file downloads carry an attachment filename.

tags.name: WebSocket
tags.description: Real-time status updates via WebSocket. Connect once at ws:///ws to receive a stream of JSON messages without polling. Requires an authenticated session cookie (Bearer token auth is not supported). Every message is the same envelope: type identifies the payload shape, payload carries it, and time is the send time in Unix milliseconds.

tags.name: Resellers
tags.description: Administrator account management and owner-scoped reseller clients, inbound grants, budgets, private plans and tokens.

tags.name: Core Configurations
tags.description: Read persisted per-core inbound configuration and validate supported documents with the installed core. Administrator write access is required.

tags.name: Activity
tags.description: Retained account-visible activity, per-user read state and current alerts. History is limited to 30 days and 10,000 events.

post.summary: Authenticate with username + password and receive a session cookie. Required before any cookie-based API call.

parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token
parameters.description: Required with a session cookie. Fetch /csrf-token under the panel base path and refresh after login. Authenticated API Bearer or mTLS requests bypass this check.

twoFactorCode.description: OTP code when 2FA is enabled. Omit otherwise.

200.description: Application result; inspect success for the outcome.

post.summary: Clear the session cookie. Requires the CSRF header for browser sessions.

parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token
parameters.description: Required with a session cookie. Fetch /csrf-token under the panel base path and refresh after login. Authenticated API Bearer or mTLS requests bypass this check.

get.summary: Mint a CSRF token for the current session. The SPA replays it in the X-CSRF-Token header on unsafe requests. Bearer-token callers can skip this — the middleware short-circuits CSRF for authenticated API requests.

post.summary: Returns whether 2FA is enabled on the panel — used by the login page to decide whether to show the OTP field.

parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token
